note: Both sets share the same core claims and the same defects: each duplicates the joist and reclaimed-surface facts, and each merges the separate labels '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE' into a single 'nut sleeve' of 1". A adds genuinely supported facts B lacks — the 2" X 8" FRAME member, the 18" landscape footing size stated without inventing an attribute, and the 3" = 1'-0" A6 scale. B's only unique claims are weaker: 'deck surface width 5 1/2"' re-binds the plywood deck's width to a vague entity, and 'landscape footing depth 18"' asserts a depth the sheet never states. A's own extras are not clean ('component width 4 1/4"' and 'decking footing plan overall depth 1'-0"' misbind detail/plan dimensions), but it still nets more correct content.
remarks: Both sets miss several real facts on the sheet: 3/4" THREADED ROD, 1" NUT (as its own item), SLEVE, 4X4 TO BE CUT AS NEEDED, the 8'-0" dimension in A6, the 3 3/4"/1 1/4" connection dims, the 7 1/2"/1 1/2"/3 1/2" plan dims, and the C1/B1/C3 scales (6"=1'-0", 1 1/2"=1'-0", 1"=1'-0"). The text layer garbles 'SLEEVE' as 'SLEVE' and runs '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE' together, which likely caused both extractors to invent a 'nut sleeve' of 1". 'LANDSCAPE FOOTING 18"' is a detail title whose 18" is ambiguous (footing size vs depth), so neither set can bind it confidently; likewise the 4 1/4" (x2) and 1'-0" dims in A6 are hard to attribute to width/thickness from the raster alone.
